text:
African American enrollment reached 30% at Taylor Elementary School for 2024-25
S. A. Leach
Taylor Elementary School counted 263 African American students in the 2024-25 school year, a decline of 1.9% from the prior year, according to the Georgia Department of Education.
During the 2024-25 school year, the school enrolled a total of 878 students, with African American students making up 30% of the total student population—the school's second-largest group by size.
The school operates within the Gwinnett County School District, which has district offices based in Lawrenceville.
Of the 140 schools in the Gwinnett County School District, Grayson High School posted the highest number of African American students for 2024-25, enrolling 2,089.
Data from the National Center for Education Statistics indicates public school enrollment in Georgia was about 36.4% Black, 35.9% white, 18.1% Hispanic, 4% Asian, 4.6% multiracial, 0.2% American Indian or Alaska Native, and 0.1% Pacific Islander.
Chronic absenteeism continues to be a challenge in Georgia schools after the pandemic, with 20.7% of students missing at least 10% of school days in 2024, according to the Georgia Department of Education. To address this, GaDOE started a statewide effort offering a real-time attendance dashboard, a public awareness plan, and focused support in high-need districts to raise daily attendance rates.
By 2025, Georgia lawmakers revised school attendance policy to prohibit expulsion based solely on absenteeism. The legislation also introduced expanded reporting obligations and aligns with existing programs that assist students in earning diplomas through alternative options.
As of 2026, Georgia reported an average student-to-teacher ratio of roughly 14:1, which is lower than the national average of 15:1.
Note: Due to potential gaps in the available data, reported percentages may not total exactly 100%.
